status_summary: Sunset provisions are operative for some energy regulators and no commission was found. Executive Order 14270 (signed 2025-04-09, 90 FR 15643) directs EPA, DOE, FERC, NRC and certain Interior and Army Corps components to add conditional sunset dates to covered existing regulations and to give new covered rules sunset dates no more than five years out. FERC published a direct final rule on 2025-10-21 (90 FR 48397), effective 2025-12-05, under which 53 listed regulations cease to have effect on 2026-12-05 unless extended, and the NRC published a direct final rule on 2025-12-03 (90 FR 55621) whose effective date of 2026-01-08 it confirmed on 2026-01-08, with listed provisions sunsetting one year later unless extended. Executive Orders 14192 (ten-for-one repeal) and 14219 (review of all regulations) do not provide sunsets or a commission, and no presidentially appointed Regulatory Reduction Commission or annual repeal package to Congress was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14270 (signed 2025-04-09) on zero-based regulatory budgeting with conditional sunset dates was published.
FERC published a direct final rule (90 FR 48397), effective 2025-12-05, adding a conditional sunset date of 2026-12-05 to 53 regulations.
NRC published a direct final rule adding conditional sunset dates to listed regulations, effective 2026-01-08 unless significant adverse comments were received.
NRC confirmed the 2026-01-08 effective date of its sunset rule, withdrawing one aircraft impact assessment amendment.

title: Ease trade adjustment with regulatory sunsets and a Regulatory Reduction Commission
uncertainties: DOE published a related zero-based regulating rule on 2026-05-29 and EPA and the Interior and Army Corps components were not checked in the Federal Register text. Whether the FERC rule took effect without significant adverse comment was not confirmed beyond a later partial rescission notice effective 2026-01-20 seen in search results. Executive Orders 14192 and 14219 are context for deregulation. The match is partial because the sunsets cover regulations of named energy agencies, not new regulations generally, and are not framed as trade adjustment measures.
